messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — idea for onboarding: run a tiny deterministic golden-probe plus a lightweight fuzz sweep in parallel, then a full bench only if either flags. aim = reduce bench cost for 80% of models. thoughts?
Samir Patel: sounds promising. can you sketch the flow?
Maya Chen: flow: 1) sanity tokenization + output shape check (fast) 2) golden-probe (10 curated prompts, compare logits/decoding fingerprints) 3) fuzz-sweep (randomized short prompts for safety/crash detection) 4) if golden or fuzz shows delta > threshold -> full bench with end-to-end latency + regression evals.
Elena Gomez: two quick concerns: tokenizer variants and sampling nondeterminism. golden-probe needs deterministic decoding seeds or fingerprinting that tolerates soft diffs.
Ravi Kumar: +1. Also: what are the thresholds? we need a metric that's cheap to compute on the probe — maybe token-by-token KL over the golden set and a structural diff score for outputs.
Maya Chen: proposal: for golden probe use ngram-jaccard of top-k tokens per step + avg token KL under greedy logits. thresholds: KL>0.08 or jaccard<0.7 triggers bench. fuzz-sweep: any runtime exception or >5% invalid tokens triggers bench. open to better numbers.
Samir Patel: those thresholds are reasonable as a starting point. We should record false-positive rate on historical models before enforcing. can benchbot run a retrospective pass? @benchbot run:retrospective --since=2023-01 --mset=approved_models
benchbot: queued retrospective job 1423. will post summary in ~45m. (react :hourglass:)
Elena Gomez: about tokenizer variants: add a quick tokenizer-compat step: run sample inputs and assert identical token counts + identical special token mapping for common tokens. if mismatch, mark as "tokenizer-variant" and route to devreview instead of automatic bench.
Ravi Kumar: we also need to consider KV cache interface compatibility. Some exported models have different past_key shapes. Add a tiny runtime check that runs a 2-step prefix+continuation and inspects k/v shapes. if mismatch -> fail fast.
Maya Chen: good call. update flow: insert kv-check after tokenization and before golden probe.
Samir Patel: rollout strategy: feature-flag this per-namespace. start opt-in for new models, run retrospective logs to pick false pos/neg and then flip default after 2 weeks. also expose a per-model override to force full bench.
Elena Gomez: monitoring: surface three signals in console: probe-fail-rate, fuzz-exception-rate, bench-trigger-rate. add a heatmap of KL/jaccard distribution so we can tune thresholds.
Ravi Kumar: cost estimate? if probe+fuzz are <=5% of a full bench compute we win if bench-skip rate >50%. need numbers.
Maya Chen: rough calc: golden (10 prompts) ~0.3% of bench; fuzz-sweep (100 short inquiries) ~1.5%. overhead negligible. retrospective should give us bench-skip estimate.
benchbot: retrospective complete. summary: on 98 models: probe-only would have skipped full bench for 62 models, would have missed 2 regressions (these were degenerate seed-related diffs). attaching short csv in #eng-ml artifacts.
Samir Patel: nice. for the 2 misses we need deterministic decoder seeds in golden probe as Elena said. also add a small ensemble check: run greedy+sampling seeds and compare stable tokens.
Elena Gomez: implementation notes: place probe and fuzz as lightweight steps in ingest lambda (5s budget). full bench remains async job on bench-cluster. add a new schema field in model registry: "onboard_probe_fingerprint" to store golden fingerprints for drift checks across versions.
Ravi Kumar: agree. and add a clear path for manual review: a single-click "request manual vet" in console when probe flags.
Maya Chen: i'll draft an RFC with flow diagram, thresholds, rollout plan, and metrics to collect. tagging @samir @elena for review. thanks all. :thumbsup:
